parameters.content:
## Google Sheets delivery queue → Prooftask → Slack
For automation consultants handing completed client work to a responsible reviewer. Reads rows marked YES, checks required material mappings against the current agreement, saves a retry-safe job, writes its ID back and reminds the team. It stops before submission.

### Setup (n8n 2.39.8)
1. Create a Google Sheet using the sample CSV in the linked setup guide. One unique task_id per intended delivery revision.
2. Set spreadsheetId, numeric sheetId and slackChannelId in Configuration.
3. Select the SAME Google Sheets OAuth2 credential on every Google Sheets node (read/write access).
4. Select a Prooftask Header Auth credential on all three HTTP nodes: Authorization = Bearer <project-scoped Agent token>. The owner must grant the existing project and SUBMIT_MATERIALS action.
5. Select a Slack credential with chat:write and add its bot to the chosen review channel.
6. Enter actual project/criterion IDs and original links in the sheet; set ready_for_review=YES. Run manually, one execution at a time.

Requires existing agreed Prooftask projects, a Prooftask account/Agent grant, Google Sheets and Slack. Respective service pricing applies. No community node installation is needed.

## Prepare real materials, not sample payloads
Input columns: task_id, ready_for_review, project_id, summary, materials_json. Operational columns: request_id, request_json, job_id, handover_state, handover_note, prepared_at, notified_job_id.

Use the sample CSV and setup guide below. materials_json is an array with criterionId, summary, references and files, one entry per current agreed criterion. Material links are not fetched or judged.

Invalid rows receive actionable NEEDS_INPUT/NEEDS_OWNER feedback. Other rows can continue. Duplicate task IDs stop the run before any writes. YES means prepare a job for internal review; it never authorizes submission or acceptance.

Setup + fictional sample CSV:
https://github.com/cognitive-emergence/prooftask-integrations/blob/main/n8n/DELIVERY_QUEUE.md

## Keep the original business process
The scoped Agent reads the existing authorized project. Current agreed criteria must match material IDs exactly. A missing permission, human pause or changed agreement produces owner feedback. No agreement, invitation or new business authority is created.

The preparation endpoint saves the exact envelope server-side. The sheet retains its opaque job ID and retry identity. A saved job is not a submitted delivery, accepted result, signature or payment.

Never run overlapping manual executions against the same queue. Keep sheet access limited to the delivery team and protect its original-material references.

## Persist BEFORE calling Prooftask
The exact request_id and request_json are written and read back before the first preparation attempt. A timeout is retried with the same identity and identical body. Edited inputs under the saved identity are blocked; use a new task row for a deliberate new revision.

If preparation succeeds but sheet writeback fails, rerun from the queue: the same saved request returns the same server job. If the reminder fails, the saved job is read instead of preparing a new delivery. Already-submitted jobs are marked separately.

Do not clear request_id/request_json to escape an error. AUTH errors require the owner; replacement Agent grants cannot silently inherit saved jobs. HTTP success never means buyer acceptance.

## End at a useful human handoff
The queue records PREPARED and an authorized team channel receives the saved job/project references. Review the exact materials, then use the existing separate send-job workflow with confirmed:true. Only the authorized buyer can record acceptance.

The Slack reminder contains no material contents. Link previews and Slack mentions are disabled. Once notified_job_id is saved, normal reruns skip the row. An uncertain Slack response or failed reminder-marker write can produce a duplicate reminder; job creation remains replay-safe.

### Customize
Map your own upstream task fields into the documented queue columns, or replace the final Slack node with an equivalent internal notification. Preserve exact IDs, scoped credentials, durable request snapshots and explicit decision boundaries. All HTTP destinations stay fixed HTTPS, with redirects disabled.

Operational data remains in your Google Sheet and Prooftask. Configure access/retention in both services. n8n execution-data saving is disabled; that does not replace your administration controls.
